title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll landed on Leaded Light. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Leaded Light
options.lineage: Modern abstract leaded glass, translated away from church windows: no figures, no crosses, faith carried by the words
options.thesis: Medieval glass was made from sand and beechwood ash; the site is built like a window, distinct panes held by strong lines and lit from behind.
options.viewport: A tall abstract window of cobalt, amber and clear panes glows at right; headline, Ask for help and Refer someone sit on a clear pane at left.
options.risk: Stained glass is the most church-coded material there is; set timidly or figuratively it becomes the bulletin the founder wants to avoid.

raised.raise: Amber is the control: in the interface, gold glass marks only what someone can press, such as Ask for help, Refer and Give.
Every block of copy is sized to its pane, and panes stack in courses down the page; no text floats free.
No flat fills: each colored pane carries its glass's own seeds and streaks, so no two panes match, the way no two people do.
One lit pane always says where you are, shared by the five-step process and the multi-step request form.
How it works is drawn as the glazier's cartoon: numbered, ruled, plain mechanics beside the finished window.

options.label: Ash & Cobalt
options.lineage: Carolina ash-glazed stoneware and cobalt-decorated salt glaze (Catawba Valley, Seagrove)
options.thesis: Carolina potters glaze stoneware with wood ash, and the kiln's fire turns that ash to glass; the site feels fired, not printed.
options.viewport: One large stoneware jar with amber ash runs anchors the hero; cobalt brushwork underlines the headline and Ask for help.
options.risk: Warm earthen craft sits near the cream-and-serif look most sites in this category land on, and can read as an artisan boutique.

options.label: Kind Interface
options.thesis: The ministry as a friendly, thumb-first app: soft cards, plain words, one amber action color.
options.viewport: Headline and Ask for help at left; stacked cards for next steps and ways to help at right; a thumb bar on phones.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and is the clearest for help-seekers on phones; loses on standing out and on saying Christian surgical ministry at a glance.
options.risk: Looks like any app, so the ministry's faith and seriousness rest on the words alone.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One gold cord pulled, and a flat cloth rises into a protective shell.
options.viewport: A black silk semicircle that gathers around the headline when the gold Ask for help cord is pulled.
options.case: Fuses poorly: couture transformation reads as cosmetic before-and-after, the look the founder ruled out.
options.kept: Gold appears only where someone can act.
options.risk: Glossy fashion register that reads as aesthetic-surgery marketing.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: The ministry raised course by course, each coil pressed by hand.
options.viewport: A coil tower rises beside a slab-capital headline; the process steps are its courses.
options.case: Fuses partly: the process maps to courses, but terracotta leaves the founder's navy and gold, and patients won't see themselves in an earthwork.
options.kept: Each text block's measure is set by its pane, stacked in courses.
options.risk: Reads as an art installation, not a place to ask about surgery.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.thesis: Each person as a one-copy print, combed in floating color and lifted once.
options.viewport: A marbled bath fills the hero; a stylus stroke reveals the headline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a fluid simulation burdens phones and screen readers and hides the request.
options.kept: No flat fills: every pane carries its own texture, so no two are alike.
options.risk: Heavy canvas work on weak connections, and the meaning stays abstract.

options.label: Rhythm Step Row
options.thesis: Sixteen lit keys and a chase light that always says where now is.
options.viewport: The five-step process as a lit step row under a tempo readout.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a toy-instrument tone is wrong for people asking about surgery.
options.kept: One lit pane always marks where you are in the process and the form.
options.risk: Playful to the point of disrespect for this audience.

options.label: Sign Shop Elevation
options.thesis: The working drawing beside the lit sign, every lamp numbered.
options.viewport: A tall roadside sign stacks the ministry's services like motel tenants.
options.case: Fuses poorly: roadside commerce cheapens a medical ministry.
options.kept: Show each promise beside its plain mechanics, like a working drawing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A hopeful ministry site done well: warm photo hero, navy and gold, serif headline, value icons, audience cards.
canonCard.viewport: A warm photograph fills the hero behind the headline and two buttons; six value icons sit below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every ministry site and depends on photos that don't exist yet.
